transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Monday, October 26. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to govt than needed, says Justice Kaul. Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has expressed concerns about how former Chief Justice D Y Chandrachud dealt with the government. He believes Chandrachud was too lenient during the process of judicial appointments, which raises worries about the independence of the judiciary. This could potentially undermine the separation between the courts and the government, according to Kaul. From outranking Fab Four to fight for place: Rise, reign and unraveling of Labuschagne. Labuschagne has been afforded more chances than most, but Australian cricket has a history of punishing batters whose judgement deserts them against South Africa. BJP calls for nationwide protest over Kharge's 'baap' remark. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's comment about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's father sparked widespread outrage among BJP members. Following the incident, the BJP announced nationwide protests against Kharge's remarks, labeling them indecent and offensive. Union home minister Amit Shah criticized Congress for personal attacks and blamed it on their electoral disappointments. Kharge also condemned the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, describing it as a threat to democracy. Nasa's Isaacman shares Artemis IV update as SpaceX, Blue Origin plan Moon base. NASA administrator Jared Isaacman provided an update regarding the Artemis III lunar mission and upcoming docking exercises. The agency plans for significant interactions with Elon Musk's SpaceX and Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin next year. Docking practices will involve astronaut teams launching aboard NASA's Orion capsule from Cape Canaveral. Isaacman indicated that the competition has intensified due to historical precedents set by earlier space missions. Alabama lawyer quit practice to care for parents; court voids her condo deed. The Alabama Supreme Court has affirmed a lower court's ruling that invalidated a property transfer from parents to their daughter, Holly Schumpert. Despite her dedication in caring for her ailing parents, the court determined the coastal condominium was part of a family trust, rendering the deed null. As a result, laws designed to protect elderly property owners allowed the reversal, leading to Holly having no claim to the estate. Brazil's Lula wins re-election, defeating Trump ally Bolsonaro. Brazil's president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was re-elected after defeating conservative challenger Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday's presidential runoff, the country's electoral authority announced, keeping Latin America's largest economy under left-wing leadership. Serbia's Vucic concedes defeat as student-led movement wins parliamentary election. Tens of thousands of people flooded the streets of Serbia's capital on Sunday night, bringing traffic to a halt and celebrating after long-time leader Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in parliamentary elections to a student-backed opposition movement. 80-ton boulder at NH Polar Caves since 1922 collapses, no injuries. In a surprising turn of events on October 18, 2026, an 80-ton granite boulder collapsed at Polar Caves Park in Rumney, New Hampshire, smashing a wooden walkway and its safety rails. Fortunately, this incident resulted in no injuries. The boulder's fall is likely due to weather-related erosion. Park authorities are now assessing the situation and implementing repair plans to allow for a safe return of visitors in spring 2027. Husband jailed next door missed hearing, lost home; court reopens case. A Kansas appeals court recently vacated a previous ruling in a divorce property case, asserting that Scott L. Hale was not given a fair chance to participate. Haltingly unable to attend his hearing due to incarceration, Scott's objections to the property division were overlooked by the trial judge. The court's decision sends the matter back to the lower court for a comprehensive reassessment and new hearing. Woman dreamt collector, built trust aiding goldsmiths, students, trans housing. M Padmavathi founded the Community Renovation and Organisation Advancement Trust to promote economic empowerment in her community. This organization aids goldsmiths, underprivileged children, and transgender individuals in securing financial stability. Between 2015 and 2020, around 4,200 students benefited from after-school coaching programs, while initiatives also aimed at connecting transgender individuals with government resources and employment opportunities. Her dedication illustrates a profound commitment to uplift lives and nurture self-sufficiency.

transcript.title: Business and markets
transcript.text: Moving to business, the economy and the markets. Capital shifting from secondary market to rupees 5 trillion IPO pipeline: Madhu Lunawat. Founder of The Wealth Company Mutual Fund Madhu Lunawat said perceived 10-12 percent inflation is pushing retail funds into small- mid-caps, and that high valuations and currency depreciation are keeping FIIs cautious. SI Arena debuts at BFSI Summit: Bringing market experts closer to investors. This year's edition introduces the Smart Investor (SI) Arena, a dynamic space crafted to empower retail and next-gen investors to make sharper financial moves. Infosys's huge deal wins fail to give it an edge over peers. Robust $5.2 billion deal wins in Q2 couldn't prevent Infosys from trimming its full-year growth outlook, leaving it trailing key competitors. Senco Gold to acquire 68 percent stake in August Jewellery for rupees 68 crore. Senco Gold Ltd on Sunday said it has signed agreements to acquire a 68 per cent stake in August Jewellery Pvt Ltd, which operates the 'Melorra' brand, for rupees 68 crore. The investment will be made in multiple tranches, with completion targeted by February 2027, subject to fulfilment of specified conditions, the company said in a regulatory filing. It said that including the acquisition by a promoter group entity, the overall stake in August Jewellery will reach 79 per cent, following which the company will become a subsidiary of Senco Gold. The investment will happen through fresh equity issuance, with the funds intended for the company's growth and expansion, and the discharge of existing liabilities, the filing said. Gold, silver face fresh test as oil surge puts Fed policy decision in focus. Gold and silver are expected to face fresh headwinds next week as surging crude oil prices revive inflation concerns, while the US Federal Reserve's policy decision could determine whether bullion rates stabilise or extend their downward trend, analysts said. The precious metals, already battered by elevated bond yields and a stronger dollar, will look to the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting and its chair's commentary for signals on whether interest rates could stay higher for longer. The focus will also be on policy decisions from the European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan, along with US durable goods orders, consumer confidence, Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation and third-quarter GDP data. Eurozone inflation readings, developments around the US mid-term elections, Russia-Ukraine peace talks and the West Asia conflict will also remain on the radar, they added. Bond yields rise nearly 30 bps in Oct, to raise govt's interest burden. The sharp rise in government bond yields since the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) October monetary policy review threatens to increase the government's borrowing costs and put pressure on its interest expenditure, potentially squeezing fiscal flexibility, according to experts. Yield on the 10-year benchmark government bond rose to 7.474 per cent on October 23 from 7.193 per cent on October 6, increasing about 28 basis points, according to data compiled by PTI. The rise in yields has been driven by elevated crude oil prices, a spike in global bond yields, tighter liquidity conditions in the Indian banking system and expectations of more interest rate hikes by the RBI, market experts said. "If yields remain elevated, the cost of financing the fiscal deficit will rise, adding pressure on interest expenditure and fiscal flexibility," said V Ramachandra Reddy, head of treasury at Karur Vysya Bank. Nifty slide brings 18 month old support back to the fore. Analyst sets sights on last April's low of 21,743.65 as a crucial support for the Nifty 50 amid worsening macros and geopolitical headwinds Top 10 firms lose rupees 1.55 trillion in mcap as HDFC Bank, Bajaj Finance fall. The combined market valuation of eight of the top 10 most valuable firms fell by rupees 1.55 lakh crore last week, with HDFC Bank and Bajaj Finance accounting for most of the losses. In a holiday-truncated week, the 30-share BSE Sensex tumbled 1,605.44 points, or 2.15 per cent, while the 50-share NSE Nifty slumped 546.15 points, or 2.36 per cent. Tracking the weak trend in equities, the total market capitalisation of BSE-listed firms fell by rupees 20,78,774.28 crore over four sessions to rupees 4,51,83,393.14 crore from rupees 4,72,62,167.42 crore recorded on October 16. Among the top 10 listed companies, eight lost rupees 1,55,671.9 crore, while two, Tata Consultancy Services and Larsen and Toubro, closed the week with valuation gains. Five companies, including EAAA India Alternatives, SFC Environmental Technologies, and M K Sons Fine Jewels, are set to launch their initial public offerings (IPOs) next week, seeking to raise close to rupees 2,600 crore from the primary market. BLS Polymers and Bombay Coated and Special Steels would also float their maiden public offerings during the week. Separately, several other companies, including Gujarat Victory Forging, Milestone Gears, Avaada Electro, Swara Baby Products, Integris Medtech and AGS Health, are in the pipeline for IPO, according to merchant bankers. These companies are expected to announce price band declarations and launch plans by November 5, ahead of the extended Diwali holiday period in Gujarat, where markets and business activity are likely to be affected by the post-Diwali observance of Labh Pancham from November 6 to 15, they added.
